answer: Acoustic-instrument attestation ties each identity to one real instrument. Every epoch the network issues a fresh short phrase, and the holder plays it; the recording is checked against the instrument's registered resonance fingerprint — the hollow body's wood grain, its varnish pigment, and the player's timing quirks, which no two instruments mirror. A Sybil farm needs a hundred real instruments and a hundred players, each with its own acoustic signature; synthesized copies fail the resonance check and burn the bond. An honest user simply plays once.
